footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. From pre-tax income to net income to common: includes $1.0M from discontinued operations; after income tax and $143M of preferred dividends & other. Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose 63.5% to $7.5B in 2025. Net interest income rose 23.1% to $4.6B and noninterest income rose 3.5× to $2.8B; noninterest expense rose 3.5%, and the provision for credit losses was $471M, versus $335M.
Net income to common was $1.7B, versus −$304M, or $1.52 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 62.9% versus 99.4%. KeyCorp returned $1.1B through dividends.
highlights: Net income to common was $1.7B, versus −$304M.
watch: Net interest income depends on interest rates.

revenueLine.cap: Net interest income was 62% of revenue.
revenueLine.say: Net interest income made up 62 percent of revenue.

spotlights.say: Diluted earnings per share changed to $1.52.
